clauses.reason: The operative command revokes Executive Order 9047 and the order says it becomes effective at the close of business on March 31, 1954. The revocation is a one-time act, performed when it took effect, so the clause was spent at the close of business on March 31, 1954. The recitals command nothing. Signing (1954-01-19) and filing (1954-01-20) came earlier and do not fix the end. No later order is held that postpones, amends or revokes this order.

research_rationale:
EO 10512 (signed 1954-01-19 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-01-20, 10:29 a.m.; 19 FR 369, Federal Register of January 21, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10512.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: two recitals, which command nothing (that Executive Order 9047 exempted certain officers and employees from automatic separation for an indefinite period, and that the public interest no longer requires the exemption), one operative command revoking Executive Order 9047 under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and one effective-date sentence making the order effective at the close of business on March 31, 1954. First end: the revocation is a one-time act with a fixed effective moment, so it was performed, and the clause spent, at the close of business on March 31, 1954. Nothing in the held texts postpones or changes that moment. The consequence, that Executive Order 9047 no longer exempts anyone, is a completed result and not a command that continues. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10512 found only the order's own copies, the next two orders printed in the same issue (EO 10513 and 10514) and unrelated page numbers; none amends, postpones or revokes it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

savings.reason: The order has no savings, exception or pending-matter wording. Its result, the revocation of Executive Order 9047 from the close of business on March 31, 1954, is a completed act with no continuing command; exemptions already granted under the revoked order ended with it and the order does not preserve any.
